primary_issue: The shatter event is not readable or energetic (no clear radial fracture or outward shard burst), and the hero action (large window + brick impact) is obscured by composition and darkness.
issues: Shatter lacks impact: shards appear as a small, dark cluster with little sense of explosive outward motion or tumbling pieces catching light.
Scene staging does not match the brief: a large single-pane window in a rusted steel frame set into an aged concrete wall is not clearly established/readable.
The brick is not clearly identifiable as a heavy red clay brick entering from frame left and passing through the center of the pane.
Composition blocks the action: a large dark foreground slab dominates the frame and the shatter occupies too little screen space to read instantly.
Lighting is under-motivated and too dim for glass readability; shards don’t get crisp specular highlights/edge sparkle, so the effect looks muddy.
Environment looks like low-detail blockout (flat materials, minimal set dressing); lacks derelict warehouse realism (grime, rust breakup, concrete wear).
Glass breakup detail is insufficient: too few/chunky pieces; no convincing fracture pattern, attached cracked remnants, or edge-collapse behavior visible.
Noticeable noise/grain on lit surfaces suggests insufficient sampling/denoising for a dark scene.
Overall color/contrast is overly crushed in the shadows, losing important story beats around the impact zone.
Compared to an internal warehouse window-shatter reference, this render is far below in framing clarity, fracture detail, material fidelity, and cinematic lighting.
suggestions: Reframe/recompose so the window and impact point are the hero (impact should fill ~30–50% of frame). Remove/raise the foreground obstruction and move the camera closer/lower.

Increase overall scene illumination and motivated keys so glass can read in darkness; specifically raise background/world intensity (Line 274: bg.inputs['Strength'] from 0.08 → ~0.25–0.6) and adjust exposure so blacks aren’t crushing the action.

Make the glass material read more physically: keep metallic at 0 (Line 131), and consider slightly increasing roughness only if highlights are noisy (Line 154: 0.015 → ~0.02–0.04) while ensuring strong, clean reflections.
Reduce overly strong green tint if it’s muddying the shards: lower absorption density (Line 164: 0.12 → ~0.03–0.08) and/or neutralize absorption color (Line 163) for clearer shard readability.
Add subtle micro-surface breakup to help specular sparkle: increase bump strength a bit (Line 128) and tune noise scale (Line 120) so glass isn’t perfectly CG-smooth, but avoid heavy distortion.
If emission is contributing to a non-photoreal look, keep it minimal/disabled for realism (Line 178: emission strength → 0 or very low). Use lighting instead of glowing glass.

Increase fracture/shard resolution and drive higher initial shard velocity + angular spin (simulation/fracture settings, not in the listed material params): you need a clear radial crack pattern + wide debris spread from the impact point, plus remaining cracked glass still attached to the frame that collapses later.
Improve set realism (beyond current material params): add rusted steel frame detail, aged concrete texture variation, grime, and industrial dressing; right now it reads too geometric and empty.
Address render noise with higher samples/denoising (render settings), especially because dark scenes amplify grain.
Add motion cues if this is part of an animation (motion blur on brick/shards, directional debris spread from left-to-center impact) so the event reads as high-speed and violent.
vision_assessment: The image reads as a very dark, low-detail industrial interior with a small, unclear window area and a faint cluster of broken-glass-like pieces near it. The main story beat—brick entering from the left, striking the center of a large pane, and producing an outward explosive shatter with sparkling tumbling shards—is not clearly visible. The window/frame/wall context is ambiguous (doesn’t convincingly read as a large single pane in a rusted steel frame set into aged concrete), and a large dark foreground shape blocks much of the frame, pushing the action into a small, hard-to-see region. Lighting is not shaped to reveal glass: there are no strong specular edge highlights or readable fracture lines, so the effect looks muddy rather than crisp and cinematic. Compared against an internal warehouse window-shatter reference, the render is far behind in composition clarity, fracture detail, material realism, and overall cinematic impact.
